items.title: Touch: dragging inside a menu dismisses the open submenu instead of scrolling
items.body: Type: Bug On a touch screen, dragging a finger inside a menu that has an open submenu dismisses the submenu instead of scrolling. Since a drag is the only way a touch user can scroll, any menu item below the fold of a submenu is unreachable by touch: the gesture for scrolling is the gesture for dismissal. ### Steps to reproduce 1. Open VS Code Web (or the desktop workbench with device emulation + touch) on a small viewport, so the menu bar collapses into the hamburger button and menus get a constrained max-height. 2. Tap the hamburger, then tap **File** so its submenu opens. On a phone-sized viewport the File submenu overflows and shows a scrollbar. 3. Drag a finger vertically inside the menu. **Actual:** the submenu closes at the first drag and focus returns to the parent item. Repeating the drag never scrolls. **Expected:** the drag scrolls the submenu; the submenu closes only when the parent menu has actually scrolled. ### Root cause Three pieces interact, all reproducible on current `main` (32b97f54e2ec0341c32d665e1f6f136db29cfe79): 1. `Gesture.dispatchEvent` delivers a gesture to **every** registered target that contains the initial touch point. A submenu is rendered as a DOM descendant of the parent menu's action item (`SubmenuMenuActionViewItem.createSubmenu`), and both the parent menu and each action item register gesture targets, so one finger movement inside the submenu also reaches the parent menu's `Gesture.Change` handler, which calls `setScrollPosi

items.title: Support Alt+click to open links beside the originating panel
items.body:
## Feature request

Support **Alt+click to open a link in an editor to the side of the current panel/editor group**, leaving the originating view visible.

## Motivation

When exploring links in a chat response, opening a linked resource in the same editor group can replace the response being used as context. For example, clicking a GitHub issue link in a chat response can open the issue editor in place of the chat. It should be possible to explicitly open the linked resource beside the source instead.

## Proposed behavior

- Alt+click on a link opens its target in an editor group to the side of the group containing the clicked link.
- Keep the originating panel/view visible and unchanged.
- Reuse an appropriate adjacent editor group where possible instead of creating another split on every click.
- Preserve ordinary-click behavior.
- Propagate the side-opening intent through link handlers and contributed openers, including targets rendered as webview/custom editors, such as GitHub issue editors.
- Leave external-browser-only targets unaffected when they cannot be opened inside VS Code.

The placement should be relative to the view containing the clicked link, not an unrelated previously active editor group.

## Example

With a chat response containing a GitHub issue link visible, Alt+click the issue. The issue opens in an editor beside the chat, so both the response and the issue remain visible.

items.title: UI dropdown menus render behind the main application window after toggling Developer Tools
items.body:
### Type
Bug

### Description
After opening the Developer Tools, inspecting elements, and maximizing the Developer Tools view, closing or switching back to the main VS Code window breaks the Z-index/window layering of top-bar dropdown menus. Menu items render behind the main editor window instead of in the foreground.

### Environment
* **VS Code Version:** 1.88+
* **OS:** Windows 10 / 11 (Git Bash terminal)
* **Extensions Disabled:** Yes (`code --disable-extensions`)

### Steps to Reproduce
1. Launch VS Code with extensions disabled (`code --disable-extensions`).
2. Open Developer Tools (`Help` > `Toggle Developer Tools` or press `F12`).
3. Maximize or expand the Developer Tools window to full screen.
4. Close the Developer Tools window (`F12` or click `X`).
5. Click on any menu item in the top menu bar (e.g., `File`, `Edit`, `Selection`, `View`).

### Expected Result
The dropdown menu opens directly below the clicked item, fully visible in the foreground on top of the main VS Code window.

### Actual Result
The dropdown menu renders behind the main application window, hiding the menu choices behind the editor interface.

Steps to Reproduce:

1. Open the Agents Window on macOS with a detail editor at the right edge.
2. Dock the secondary sidebar in the editor, or open an integrated browser in the rightmost editor group.
3. Inspect the bottom-right corner in both Default and Compact layout density.

items.title: Editor Window Chat: section bar "more" needs to be double clicked to expand/collapse
items.body:
Version: 1.142.0-insider
Commit: ed380adfe6e65ec56c354a49622b844af3938878
Date: 2026-10-09T04:19:40Z
Electron: 43.7.7
ElectronBuildId: 15553055
Chromium: 150.0.7871.250
Node.js: 24.21.0
V8: 15.0.245.31-electron.0
@github/copilot: 1.0.95-0
@github/copilot-sdk: 1.0.19-preview.0
OS: Darwin arm64 25.6.0

1. Open a workspace in an Editor Window
2. Open chat
3. You need at least 4 chats in your chat history -> at least one of your chats is in the More section
4. Single-click the More section title, nothing happens, I need to double-click to collapse/expand the section. In the Agents Window this works with single-click
